subject: armadillo girdled lizard
title: This Lizard Survives Meerkats by Biting Its Own Tail

scenes.text: When meerkats attack this lizard, it bites itself.
The armadillo girdled lizard lives among the rocks of western South Africa, covered in spiny armoured scales.
Its only soft spot is its belly. Meerkats and mongooses know it.
So it grabs its own tail in its jaws and rolls into a spiky ring, belly hidden inside.
It can hold that ball for up to an hour. Most attackers give up.
The weak spot is the sky. Spines don't stop a hawk's talons.

description:
The armadillo girdled lizard of South Africa defends itself by gripping its own tail in its jaws and rolling into an armoured ball that protects its soft belly.
Camera traps found meerkats and small grey mongooses were its most frequent ground predators; the armour is thought to be far less useful against birds of prey.

first_comment: These lizards live in groups of up to 60 in one rock crack. Which animal defence is the weirdest you know?
